not_upheld.2: Völuspá's 'drepr hann af móði' (the diplomatic text writes mæði) is usually read 'in wrath'; 'in fury' stands.
not_upheld.9: 'mit ir kraft' as 'in their power' (might) is a defensible reading; 'with their retinue' is another.
not_upheld.14: Dante's 'torto' as 'twisted' is defensible (Longfellow has 'contorted'); 'scowling' is another reading.
not_upheld.15: Upheld in part: 'aimme' is third person, so it is God (just named in the oath) who loves right, not Oberon. The line now reads 'who greatly loves', which makes that plain.
